releases.title: Ideas built on your draft

highlights.title: Your draft leads
highlights.text: Whatever you've typed or dictated becomes the heart of every comment idea.

highlights.title: Clearly marked
highlights.text: “Built on your draft” above the ideas, and the closest one is labelled.

changes: Comment ideas keep your draft's message (who it's for, what it praises, any detail or joke) and turn it into a finished comment in the tone and language you pick
Dictated drafts are tidied up: misheard names and words are corrected from the activity, and “I would like to give…” becomes a comment to your friend
After you tap an idea, ↻ and tone or language changes go back to your own draft, not the idea you picked
fixes: Comment ideas could ignore what you had already written in the box

releases.title: Before and after

highlights.title: Before and after
highlights.text: The original and the result sit side by side, each shown whole, never cropped.

highlights.title: Full screen
highlights.text: Tap a picture to see it full screen; tap again to flip between original and result.

changes: 📸 Photo with your stats: after a redesign or clean stats, the original (left) and the result (right) show side by side in the photo's own shape
Full-screen view fits the whole picture to the screen, with Original and Redesigned buttons, tap-to-compare, and Save or share
The original alone, before a redesign, is shown whole too and opens full screen
fixes: The redesigned photo showed as a cropped strip, so you couldn't see the whole result

releases.title: The redesign studio

highlights.title: Your wishes first
highlights.text: A picked photo waits for your wishes; nothing is repainted until you tap Redesign my photo.

highlights.title: A show while it paints
highlights.text: Your photo cycles through sketch, darkroom, pop art, glitch and neon effects as the AI works.

highlights.title: See the plan
highlights.text: Live steps, a progress bar, the art director's headline and stats, and running jokes.

changes: 🎨 AI redesign: a box for your wishes with one-tap ideas (retro 80s, 1970s film photo, comic hero, watercolour, neon, movie poster, funny quote) and a big Redesign my photo button right under it
Switching to 🎨 AI redesign no longer starts a redesign by itself; 📊 Clean stats still draws straight away
The redesign studio takes the whole sheet: steps (Reading the numbers, Art direction, Painting), a progress bar, the model and size, a timer and the plan (headline, stats, style)
fixes: Picking a photo started an AI redesign at once, before you could say how it should look

releases.title: Clean stats that fit

highlights.title: Stats that fit
highlights.text: 📊 Clean stats always stay inside the photo, with a margin on every side.

changes: Rows of stats wrap onto the next line instead of running past the edge, and the whole block shrinks until it fits
fixes: 📊 Clean stats with many numbers ran off the sides of the photo and cut values like the place and start time

releases.title: Your photo, redesigned

highlights.title: AI photo redesign
highlights.text: OpenAI's image model repaints your whole photo into a poster of the activity, your way.

highlights.title: Every number
highlights.text: Heart rate, cadence, power, weather, place, PRs and more: whatever makes the activity special.

highlights.title: Instructions drive it
highlights.text: Settings › Posting assistant sets the look; ask for changes like “retro 80s, add a funny quote”.

changes: Your activities › Photo with your stats: choose 🎨 AI redesign or 📊 Clean stats; both results are kept so you can switch between them
AI redesign: the AI in use art-directs from your instructions, the photo and every number of the activity, then GPT Image repaints the photo at high quality, keeping you and the place recognisable
Progress while it paints, with the step and a timer; Redesign takes your request for changes
Clean stats now shows every stat worth showing (often 6 to 10), in a grid when there are many, and reads weather, achievements and the date too
New default instructions for photos; if you never changed the old ones, they move to the new default

releases.title: Your posting assistant

highlights.title: Titles and descriptions
highlights.text: Tap your activity for title and description ideas written as you, then save them to Strava.

highlights.title: Stats on a photo
highlights.text: Pick a photo and your distance, pace and route go on it, placed the way you like.

highlights.title: Your instructions
highlights.text: Settings › Posting assistant sets the tone of your posts and the look of your photo stats.

changes: Your activities › any activity › ✍️ Posting assistant: ✨ Title & description and 📸 Stats on a photo

Ideas use everything the activity page knows: stats, splits, heart rate, weather, achievements, your photos, the current text and Strava's own insights (such as Athlete Intelligence) when the page has them
Save to Strava changes the title and description through Strava's edit form, keeping every other setting, and checks the change arrived; if Strava refuses, the text is copied to paste in Strava
Ask for something different (funnier, mention the sunset) and get new ideas; titles and descriptions stay editable before saving

Stats on a photo: from Photos, the camera or the activity's own photos; the AI looks at the photo to keep stats off faces, picks the numbers, fonts and colours from your instructions, adds the route line, and you can ask for changes; Save or share opens the share sheet
AI settings › Token usage names the new features (Titles & descriptions, Photo stats) and Comics
fixes: AI settings › Token usage showed the raw tag "comic" instead of Comics

releases.title: App Store ready

highlights.title: Ready for the App Store
highlights.text: Built as an app of its own, Daily Digest gets new versions from the App Store instead of downloading them.

highlights.title: Checked on every change
highlights.text: Every change now runs the shared app tests: start-up, widget, updates and usage counts.

highlights.title: Same buttons, any home
highlights.text: Every button in the digest, and Back to digest on Strava's page, works the same way in Scriptable and as an app of its own.

changes: In-app updates 1.1.0: in a native shell (BuildIt) there is no update check or installer, and Settings › Updates says new versions come through the App Store
Portable bridge recipe: the page, and the Back to digest button on Strava's page, hand their messages to window.__hostBridge when a native shell provides one
Testing recipe: the app-blueprints testkit (lint and five conformance packs) runs on every push (.github/workflows/tests.yml), next to the app test
Blueprint trace: Stability patterns 1.0.1, AI configuration 1.0.1, Launch screen 1.0.1, Widgets 1.1.1

releases.title: Share when you're ready

highlights.title: Share comic
highlights.text: A finished comic waits for you: tap Share comic when you want to send or save it.

highlights.title: Nothing pops up
highlights.text: The share sheet no longer opens on its own after the pages are drawn.

highlights.title: Fresh story, fresh comic
highlights.text: Rewriting the story clears the old comic's Share button.

changes: After 💥 Comic (Drawn by AI or a template look), the pages wait for 📤 Share comic in the story's footer instead of opening the share sheet

releases.title: The comic factory

highlights.title: Comic factory
highlights.text: While AI draws your comic, watch it being made: cast, locations, script, storyboard, ink, print.

highlights.title: Pages as they land
highlights.text: Each page flips over on screen the moment it's drawn, with a tick or a note if it failed.

highlights.title: A real Draw button
highlights.text: ✨ Drawn by AI now looks and feels like a button, and shows clearly when a key is missing.

changes: The factory covers the whole screen while the comic is made, with a timer, a progress bar and lines about the day's cast
Casting shows everyone's face, Locations the story's photos, Script types the story, Storyboard shows each page's real captions and speech bubbles
✨ Drawn by AI is a raised button with a Draw › pill that presses down; without an OpenAI key it is grey with No key

releases.title: Comics drawn by AI

highlights.title: Drawn by AI
highlights.text: 💥 Comic › ✨ Drawn by AI draws every page in full: panels, art, bubbles and lettering.

highlights.title: Your style, really
highlights.text: The pages follow your story instructions, so asking for a comic now gives a real comic.

highlights.title: Your friends, cartooned
highlights.text: Profile pictures and the day's photos guide how friends and places are drawn.

changes: The story's AI plans the pages (panels, captions, speech bubbles) from the story, its photos and your story instructions; OpenAI's GPT Image model draws each page
Uses the newest GPT Image model your OpenAI key can reach (gpt-image-2 by default, gpt-image-1 if that isn't available); needs an OpenAI key, also when Claude writes the story
Each page gets a slim footer with the page number and who wrote and drew it; the last one has the QR code to the app
Two pages are drawn at a time, with progress in the story sheet; all pages open in the share sheet to save to Photos
The Pop, Cool and Old paper templates stay as quick options and no longer show script markers such as [PANEL 1] or [Visual]
fixes: Comic pages showed the story's comic script as plain text in caption boxes instead of drawing it

releases.title: Early risers first

highlights.title: Early risers on top
highlights.text: The 4, 5 and 6 AM clubs lead each group, earliest first.

highlights.title: Then photos
highlights.text: People who posted photos come next, newest first.

highlights.title: Then everyone else
highlights.text: The rest follow, newest activity first.

changes: The same order in Waiting for your kudos and in Kudos given, in every layout
When the details load and show someone started early or posted photos, their line moves to its place without a redraw

releases.title: Opens on any iPhone

highlights.title: Opens on any iPhone
highlights.text: Strava Daily Digest opens on iPhones that aren't signed in to iCloud, every time.

highlights.title: Installs on new phones
highlights.text: The installer works on a brand-new iPhone without iCloud too.

highlights.title: Updates safely
highlights.text: Updating can no longer stop on a phone without iCloud.

changes: iCloud is used only when Scriptable keeps its scripts in iCloud Drive; otherwise everything stays on the phone
Settings › Built with lists Stability patterns 1.0.0, Settings 1.1.2 and In-app updates 1.0.1
fixes: On an iPhone not signed in to iCloud, Strava Daily Digest or its installer could still stop with "iCloud is not supported"

releases.title: Works without iCloud

highlights.title: Opens without iCloud
highlights.text: Strava Daily Digest now opens on iPhones that aren't signed in to iCloud.

highlights.title: Kept on the phone
highlights.text: Without iCloud, your settings are saved on the phone instead.

highlights.title: iCloud as before
highlights.text: Signed in to iCloud? Nothing changes: everything stays in iCloud Drive.

changes: Without iCloud, settings are kept in Files › On My iPhone › Scriptable
fixes: On an iPhone not signed in to iCloud, Strava Daily Digest stopped at once with "iCloud is not supported"

releases.title: Your activities, on top only

highlights.title: Not in your own feed
highlights.text: Your activities only show in Your activities on top, never as a card waiting for kudos.

highlights.title: Side by side
highlights.text: Several activities sit left to right in one card, three across; swipe for the rest.

highlights.title: Flags fixed
highlights.text: France and a few others showed as boxed letters; they show their flag now.

changes: Settings › Digest no longer has Show my own activities
👍 All never counts you
Your activities shows up to ten from today and yesterday
fixes: With Show my own activities on, your own activity waited for your kudos and the kudos failed with HTTP 403
France showed as F X boxes instead of 🇫🇷

releases.title: Delivered, then gone

highlights.title: Posting a comment finishes
highlights.text: After Delivered, the screen closes by itself again and the digest scrolls as before.

changes: The app test now posts comments in the Comfortable and Tiny layouts and checks the Delivered screen closes
fixes: Since 1.30.0 the Delivered screen stayed up after posting a comment: the comic's starburst had taken the name of its confetti

releases.title: Early-riser tags everywhere

highlights.title: On every layout
highlights.text: Comfortable and Compact now show the 4 AM, 5 AM or 6 AM tag on the profile photo too.

changes: The icon after an early riser's name is gone in every layout; the tag on the photo replaces it
Each activity keeps its own early-riser badge (for example 🌅 6 AM club) in Comfortable and Compact

releases.title: Early risers, on the photo

highlights.title: Early-riser tags on photos
highlights.text: Tiny lines show 4 AM, 5 AM or 6 AM on the profile photo's lower edge, in the club's colours.

changes: The tag uses the room already around the photo, so lines stay the same height and names get the full width
Night blue for 4 AM, violet for 5 AM, sunrise orange for 6 AM; VoiceOver and a long press name the club

releases.title: Log in works again

highlights.title: Log in to Strava works
highlights.text: The Log in to Strava button opens Strava's login again, after logging out or on a first start.

changes: A test now checks logging in, logging out and logging back in before every release, and on every change to the app
fixes: Log in to Strava and Open Strava did nothing when tapped
Try again on the start-up error page did nothing when tapped

releases.title: Log out of Strava

highlights.title: Log out in Settings
highlights.text: Settings › Account › Log out of Strava signs the app out of strava.com in two taps.

highlights.title: Switch accounts
highlights.text: The login page comes straight back, so you can sign in again or with another account.

highlights.title: Your setup stays
highlights.text: Settings, AI keys, instructions and learned style are kept; only the account is forgotten.

changes: Logging out forgets the remembered athlete ID, the cached activities and the names on the widget
If Strava keeps the phone signed in, the app opens Strava's page so you can tap Log Out there, and carries on by itself
The first tap arms the button (Log out?), the second logs out, like 👍 All

releases.title: Tidier story and weather

highlights.title: Small things, fixed
highlights.text: The story's title fits beside its language buttons, and the weather badge is easy to read.

fixes: The day's story title was cut to “The day’…” next to Auto, EN and LT
The weather badge on an activity was pale text on a pale badge
The one-tap tweaks in Settings › The day's story showed as plain text instead of buttons

releases.title: Your story, your rules

highlights.title: Instructions for the story
highlights.text: Settings › The day's story holds the story's instructions: tone, length, style. Edit them freely.

highlights.title: One-tap tweaks
highlights.text: More energetic, more specific, funnier, more dialogue, shorter, longer, gentler: tap to add, tap to take out.

highlights.title: Rewrite once
highlights.text: The same buttons under a story rewrite just that one, leaving your instructions as they are.

changes: The story's tone, length and structure now come from your instructions, which win over the app's defaults
Always kept, whatever the instructions: only real facts, every friend by first name, nobody mocked
Shorter and Longer replace each other; Reset to default brings back the original instructions
Up to 4,000 characters, with a counter, like the comment instructions

releases.title: Three looks for the comic

highlights.title: Cool
highlights.text: Dark pages, neon cyan and pink ink, sleek lettering: a modern comic.

highlights.title: Old paper
highlights.text: Yellowed paper, sepia photos, typewriter captions, coffee rings: a strip from 1955.

highlights.title: Pick before drawing
highlights.text: 💥 Comic asks for the look first and remembers the one you picked.

changes: Pop is the bright Sunday comic from 1.30, still the default
Old paper turns every photo and profile picture sepia, adds faded edges and foxing spots
Each look has its own colours for panels, captions, sound effects and THE END

releases.title: The day's story, as a comic

highlights.title: Comic pages
highlights.text: 💥 Comic turns the day's story into comic pages: a cover, panels and THE END.

highlights.title: The whole story, every time
highlights.text: Long stories run over as many pages as they need; nothing is cut off any more.

highlights.title: Save them all at once
highlights.text: The share sheet's Save Images keeps every page in Photos, ready to post later.

changes: Pages are 1080×1350, a shape Strava and Instagram show in full
The cover has the title on a sun-burst and everyone starring, with kudos rings
Each paragraph is a panel: a caption box, its photos, or the friends it mentions, and a sound effect (SPLASH!, ZOOM!, STOMP!…) picked from what happens
A paragraph too long for one panel continues in the next; spare room goes to the pictures
Up to nine of the story's photos now make it into the pages (before: three)
THE END panel carries the app's mark and the QR code; every page is numbered
fixes: A long story didn't fit the single picture and was cut off with …

releases.title: The weather, back for real

highlights.title: Weather on every outdoor line
highlights.text: When Strava keeps no weather, the app fetches the hour's weather where the activity started.

highlights.title: Country and weather together
highlights.text: Tiny lines show the country after the title and the weather above 💬.

changes: Weather comes from Open-Meteo (free, no account): only the start point, rounded to about 1 km, and the date are sent
Rain in that hour or the next counts as rain, even when the sky was mostly cloudy
Comfortable and Compact layouts show the weather as a badge too, for example 🌧️ rain, 7°, feels like 4°
Comment ideas get the same weather
Part of Load extra details: turn that off and no weather is fetched; indoor activities without a route get none
fixes: The weather chip almost never showed, because Strava rarely includes the weather in the activity's data

releases.title: Where in the world

highlights.title: The country, nothing more
highlights.text: Tiny lines show the activity's country and flag after its title, never the city.

changes: When the title is long, only the flag shows, so the title keeps its room; a long press names the country
Works when Strava writes only a city and region: the region (apskritis, novads, maakond) or the activity's time zone tells the country
Comment ideas know the country too

releases.title: Tiny lines, put to work

highlights.title: Comment from the line
highlights.text: Each Tiny line has a 💬 that opens the comment sheet straight away, no expanding.

highlights.title: The weather at a glance
highlights.text: When Strava has the weather, Tiny lines show it above 💬: rain, sun or snow, and the temperature.

changes: Weather shows as one emoji (☀️ ⛅ ☁️ 🌧️ ❄️ ⛈️ 🌫️ 💨) and the temperature; VoiceOver and a long press read it in full, feels-like included
Long names in Tiny lines end in … instead of running under the buttons

releases.title: Stories in your language

highlights.title: Your language, from the start
highlights.text: The day's story is written in the language set in Settings, not guessed from titles.

highlights.title: One tap, another language
highlights.text: Auto, EN and LT sit at the top of the story; tap one to rewrite it straight away.

changes: Settings › AI comments has Language of the day's story: Same as comments (the default), Auto, English or Lithuanian
A language tapped in the story sheet is remembered for the next story
Opening a story kept in another language writes a new one in the current language
While a story is written, the sheet says which language it is in
fixes: Changing the comment language in the composer no longer clears the highlighted story language

releases.title: LT means Lithuanian

highlights.title: Your language pick wins
highlights.text: Tap LT and every idea is in Lithuanian, even for an English title like Lunch Hike.

highlights.title: Post in the header
highlights.text: Post sits next to ✕ at the top, so the comment box gets the full width.

changes: EN and LT now override any language rule in your instructions; Auto still follows the activity title
If ideas still come back in the wrong language, the app asks once more before showing them
Post is dimmed until there is something to post, and lights up when you tap an idea
fixes: With LT picked, ideas for an English-titled activity came back in English

releases.title: Learning you can watch

highlights.title: Learning in its own window
highlights.text: Learn my style opens a window with a live count of your comments found so far.

highlights.title: Your words float up
highlights.text: Words and emojis from each comment it finds rise through the sky as it goes.

highlights.title: Hide it, keep going
highlights.text: Hide the window and keep using the app; a small pill shows progress. Just keep the app open.

changes: Learn my style runs in the background: closing Settings, changing day or refreshing no longer loses its progress
The window says plainly that closing the app or letting the phone lock stops learning
Stop, use these learns from what was found so far; a tap outside the window hides it
A ✍️ pill in the corner shows found of wanted and reopens the window; Settings shows Show progress while it runs
When it finishes with the window hidden, a short message says how many comments it learned from
fixes: Closing Settings while learning lost the result message and the Learn button stayed out of step

releases.title: Room for the sun

highlights.title: Whole sun, every time
highlights.text: While ideas are written, the sun and its rays always fit on screen, never cut at the top.

changes: The comment sheet grows while ideas are written, so the sky has room
On shorter iPhones the sun gets a little smaller instead of being cropped
If space still runs out, the sky scrolls rather than cutting anything off
fixes: The sun's rays were cut off at the top of the comment sheet when it was short

releases.title: Whole instructions

highlights.title: Nothing cut off
highlights.text: Instructions for every AI comment now take up to 4,000 characters, as promised.

highlights.title: Repaired for you
highlights.text: Instructions cut off at 2,000 characters are made whole again when the app opens.

changes: Settings › Comment writing shows how many of the 4,000 characters the instructions use
fixes: The instructions box still stopped at 2,000 characters, so pasting the new default cut it off mid-sentence
1.26.0 checked the new default instructions in the wrong place, so a first start could skip moving very old settings out of the Keychain

releases.title: Comments that notice things

highlights.title: One button to start
highlights.text: Tap ✨ Suggest comments; tone, language and ↻ sit in one tidy row to reshape the ideas.

highlights.title: See what it spots
highlights.text: While ideas are written, what the photos and data show rises up the screen as emojis.

highlights.title: Reads the whole activity
highlights.text: Weather, telemetry, the description and comments already there all shape the ideas.

changes: New default instructions for AI comments: short, casual, specific, written as if typed on a phone, in the title's language; instructions you changed are kept
Language Auto (now the default) writes in the language of the activity title; EN and LT still force a language
The composer opens on one ✨ Suggest comments button; tones show as compact emoji pills, the chosen one named, beside Auto, EN, LT and ↻
With ideas on screen, tapping a tone or language writes a fresh set straight away; the picked idea is highlighted
Photos are looked at once to name what is in them; those findings rise as emojis during writing and steer the comments
Ideas read the activity page first: elapsed and moving time, climbing, speed, cadence, power, calories, relative effort, race, device and the weather Strava stored
The comments already on the activity go with the request (yours marked), so ideas never repeat them
Your learned style and up to six of your latest posted comments go into every request, whichever tone is picked
Instructions for every AI comment can now be up to 4,000 characters
fixes: Comment ideas answered as a plain JSON list came back empty

releases.title: Clearer Settings

highlights.title: Sections you can see
highlights.text: Each Settings section now sits in its own card, so you can tell where it starts and ends.

highlights.title: Quieter headings
highlights.text: Section names are small grey capitals, so they no longer look like settings.

highlights.title: In every palette
highlights.text: The cards follow your colours, text size and layout, light or dark.

changes: Settings (app-blueprints · settings 1.1.0): each section's rows sit in one card, with a thin border and a slightly lighter background, under a small muted uppercase heading
The changed-count line and a section's explanation sit outside the cards; Built with is a card too

releases.title: Counted by name

highlights.title: Counts say which app
highlights.text: Anonymous usage counts now name Daily Digest, so they stay separate from other apps in the same place.

highlights.title: Text size respected
highlights.text: The one-time sharing question follows your text size setting.

highlights.title: Built with
highlights.text: Settings › Built with now lists Anonymous usage analytics.

changes: Every anonymous usage event carries app = stravafeed
Settings › Built with lists Anonymous usage analytics 1.1.0
fixes: The sharing question's text ignored the text size setting

releases.title: Night owl friendly

highlights.title: Yesterday after midnight
highlights.text: Open the app after midnight before anyone has posted, and it shows yesterday instead of an empty today.

highlights.title: Says so
highlights.text: A small note explains why you're looking at yesterday.

highlights.title: One tap back
highlights.text: Show today switches back whenever you like.

changes: Opening the app before 6 AM with nothing posted today shows yesterday, with a 🌙 note and a Show today button
Only when the app opens: refreshing or tapping Today later shows today as before

releases.title: Usage counts reach the project

highlights.title: Right place
highlights.text: Anonymous usage counts now go to the PostHog project's own region, the US cloud.

highlights.title: Forgets the wrong address
highlights.text: An address remembered by 1.23.1 is cleared, so nothing more is sent where it gets lost.

highlights.title: Clearer test
highlights.text: Send test now names the address PostHog accepted the event at.

changes: Settings › Privacy › Send test shows the address that accepted the event
fixes: Usage counts went to PostHog's EU cloud, which accepted and then dropped them because the project lives in the US cloud; 1.23.1's fallback never noticed, since the EU cloud said OK

releases.title: Usage counts that arrive

highlights.title: Finds the right cloud
highlights.text: Works whether the PostHog project lives in the EU or the US cloud, and remembers which.

highlights.title: Send test
highlights.text: Settings › Privacy has a Send test button that shows PostHog's answer straight away.

highlights.title: Logged
highlights.text: Every send, and any error from PostHog, is noted in the start-up log.

changes: Settings › Privacy shows when counts were last sent and whether PostHog accepted them, with a Send test button
Counts are sent after 3 seconds instead of 8
fixes: Usage counts were sent only to PostHog's EU cloud, so a project in the US cloud never received them
PostHog's answer was ignored, so a refused request looked the same as a successful one

releases.title: Help shape the app

highlights.title: Anonymous usage, if you agree
highlights.text: A one-time question asks whether to share anonymous counts, like app opens, kudos and AI features used.

highlights.title: Nothing personal
highlights.text: Only a random install ID and counts: never names, comments, photos or your Strava account.

highlights.title: Your choice, any time
highlights.text: Settings › Privacy turns it on or off; off also deletes the install ID.

changes: One-time question at the top of the digest: Yes, share or No thanks
Settings › Privacy › Share anonymous usage

When on, sends counts to PostHog's EU cloud: app opens (version, layout, theme, language, whether an AI key and a learned style exist), days viewed, kudos sent, comments posted and liked, AI ideas (mood, language, photos looked at), stories and story images made, style learning results, your own activities opened, and updates
Events are anonymous, sent in small batches, and never slow the app; if sending fails they're dropped

releases.title: Post the day's story

highlights.title: Story as a picture
highlights.text: Turn the day's story into a 1080×1920 image, ready for Instagram, with the cast, title, story and photos.

highlights.title: Scan to get the app
highlights.text: Every image carries a Made with Strava Daily Digest mark and a QR code that opens the app's GitHub page.

highlights.title: Straight to the share sheet
highlights.text: Save it to Photos or post it to Instagram from the iPhone share sheet.

changes: 📸 Image in the day's story makes a 1080×1920 picture: app logo and date, cast with kudos rings, title, the story (text size fitted to the space) and up to three of its photos
Footer with the app logo, Made with Strava Daily Digest, and a QR code to github.com/gadominas/StravaFeed (built into the app, no network needed)
Photos and profile pictures are loaded by the app so the page can draw them; the finished picture opens in the iPhone share sheet

releases.title: Sunshine while you wait

highlights.title: Your friend, shining
highlights.text: While comment ideas are written, the composer turns into a sky with your friend's photo as the sun.

highlights.title: Something to read
highlights.text: Funny lines rotate while you wait: scrambling the adjectives, cooking up something witty, pacing the punchline…

highlights.title: See how far along
highlights.text: A progress bar follows the photos being looked at and the ideas being written; Cancel if you change your mind.

changes: Tapping ✨ Suggest covers the composer with a sky: the friend's profile picture (or initials) as the sun with turning rays, drifting clouds, rotating funny lines and a progress bar
The bar follows the real steps: each photo looked at, then the ideas being written
Cancel closes the sky and ignores ideas that arrive afterwards
With Reduce Motion on, the sun and clouds stay still

releases.title: Learn my style really reads your comments

highlights.title: Opens every friend's activity
highlights.text: Learn my style no longer waits for Strava to report comments; it opens friends' activities until it finds yours.

highlights.title: Reaches further back
highlights.text: When today's activities run out it reads older weeks of your feed and keeps going.

highlights.title: Shows what it did
highlights.text: Settings and the start-up log show comments read, pages opened and how far back it reached.

changes: Settings › Learn my style always shows comments read, activities opened and the earliest day reached
Each run is noted in the start-up log, with how many comments came from Strava's data and how many from pages
fixes: Learn my style opened no pages when Strava's feed didn't report comment counts, so it learned only from comments sent through the digest

releases.title: Comments that see the photos

highlights.title: Comment ideas see the photos
highlights.text: The AI looks at up to three of the activity's photos and builds comment ideas on what it spots.

highlights.title: Reads the description
highlights.text: The whole description goes in, emojis included, so 🥐, 🌧️ or 🐶 can turn into the comment's joke.

highlights.title: Learns from all your comments
highlights.text: Learn my style now opens friends' activities one by one until it has the number you set, up to 50, with Stop.

changes: Comment ideas attach up to three of the activity's photos and ask the AI to name the objects, places, food, animals and moments it sees
The full description goes to the AI (from the activity page when the feed shortened it), with its emojis listed
The ✨ Suggest button says 📷 Looking at the photos… while it works, and the result says how many photos the AI looked at

Learn my style reads Strava's comment data first, then opens friends' activity pages one at a time (friends you gave kudos to first) and reads your comments as Strava shows them, until it has the number you set
Stop learns from what was found so far; Settings shows how many comments were read and how many activities were opened
If the chosen model can't read photos, comment ideas are written without them
fixes: Learn my style found only the comments you'd posted through the digest when Strava's comment data had none of yours

releases.title: Stories with photos

highlights.title: The AI looks at the photos
highlights.text: Up to three photos per person go into the day's story, and the AI writes about what it sees in them.

highlights.title: Photos and faces in the story
highlights.text: The cast's profile pictures sit at the top, and the photos appear right where the story talks about them.

highlights.title: Watch it come together
highlights.text: A progress bar shows athletes gathered, photos loaded and the story being written.

changes: The day's story sends up to three photos per person (twelve in all, spread so more people get one) for the AI to look at, shrunk to about 768 px
The AI places each photo under the paragraph it belongs to; tap one to open it full screen and swipe through the story's photos
Cast row with profile pictures: an orange ring for people still waiting for your kudos, green for those who have it
Progress bar with three steps: Athletes, Photos (with a count) and Looking at the photos and writing
Another take reuses the photos already loaded
If the chosen AI model can't read photos, the story is written without them and says so
fixes: Replies with line breaks inside the AI's JSON are repaired before reading

releases.title: The day's story

highlights.title: The day's story
highlights.text: Tap 📖 before Today and the AI writes one funny story starring everyone in the day's digest.

highlights.title: Kudos included
highlights.text: Everyone's in it, whether they're still waiting for your kudos or already have it, with their real activities.

highlights.title: Another take, or share
highlights.text: Not funny enough? Ask for another take, or share the story with your friends.

changes: 📖 button at the left of the day switcher writes a story about everyone in the day's digest, in one AI request, in your comment language
The story uses each person's activities (titles, sports, times, places, PRs, early starts, photos) and who has your kudos
Another take writes a fresh story; Share opens the iPhone share sheet; reopening shows the same story without asking the AI again
Route maps no longer appear on the cards; they're in the activity's details sheet
AI settings › usage lists the day's story separately
fixes: Story replies with line breaks inside the AI's JSON are read correctly

releases.title: Route maps on every card

highlights.title: See the route
highlights.text: Runs, rides and walks show their route map right on the card, between the stats and the photos.

highlights.title: Drawn when Strava sends no picture
highlights.text: When Strava only sends the route line, the digest draws it, with start and finish marked.

highlights.title: Tap for details
highlights.text: Tap the map to open the activity's details, where the same map appears.

changes: Route map on each activity card (Comfortable, and Compact or Tiny once expanded); indoor activities show none
The route is drawn from Strava's encoded route line when there is no map picture, or when the picture fails to load
The details sheet shows the card's map instead of a separate picture
fixes: The details sheet sometimes showed one of the activity's photos as its "route map"; the page preview picture is now used only when it really is a map

releases.title: Opens every time, and shows what AI adds

highlights.title: Opens every time
highlights.text: No more blank screen when opening from the widget, after quick taps or with slow iCloud.

highlights.title: See what AI adds
highlights.text: Without a key, a short card now and then shows what AI adds to your comments.

highlights.title: Start-up log
highlights.text: Settings › Updates › Start-up log shows what happened the last times it opened.

changes: The digest opens on an empty dark window first, then the launch screen, then reads its data, so a page is always drawn
Quick taps on the widget open one window, not several
Your Strava feed starts loading just after the first screen is up; the update check follows a few seconds later
Without an AI key, an invitation card appears at most every 3 days (weekly after four "Later"s), never over another sheet or an update offer; "Don't remind me again" stops it for good
Turn on AI opens AI settings with Add key highlighted; removing your last key brings the invitation back from the next launch
Settings › Updates has a Start-up log row with the last 40 lines
If a saved file turns out to be damaged, the digest keeps a copy of it, starts that file fresh and tells you so
fixes: Opening the digest could stay on a blank screen, most often from the widget or with slow iCloud
A comment history or settings file that iCloud hadn't delivered could be saved over with an empty one
If opening stalls, the screen now says so and shows the start-up log instead of staying blank
A damaged comment history or settings file no longer stops the digest from saving your changes
Turn on AI now highlights Add key for the provider in use, not always Claude's

releases.title: Learns from more of your comments

highlights.title: Finds your comments
highlights.text: Learn my style now recognises far more of your own comments among everything it reads.

changes: Settings › Learn my style shows how many comments were read on how many activities, next to how many were yours
When it finds too few, the message says how many it read and whose name it looked for
fixes: A comment's author was sometimes taken from the comment's own ID, so most of your comments weren't recognised as yours
Your name was only known when your own activities were in the loaded feed; it's now read from your Strava profile
Shortened names ("Gediminas S.") and names written with or without Lithuanian letters now match

changes: Removed the ✎ Custom mood, its prompt field in the composer and the Custom prompt setting

releases.title: Comments that sound like you

Comments you post through the digest are remembered on the iPhone (last 50) as the surest examples of your style
AI settings › usage lists style learning separately

releases.title: Your activities, on top

highlights.title: Like comments

changes: "Your activities" strip at the top of the digest: your activities from today and yesterday, newest first, up to three side by side, each with kudos and comments received

Tapping one opens a sheet with who gave kudos (with a full list) and all comments
Like or unlike a comment with its heart; the first like goes through Strava's own button and teaches the app the request, later likes are sent directly

releases.title: Kudos at a glance

highlights.text: The kudos widget now wears the Daily Digest logo on its dark tile, like the other apps.

highlights.title: Every size
highlights.text: Small, medium and large on the Home Screen, plus inline, round and rectangular on the Lock Screen.

highlights.title: Never an error

changes: Home Screen widget in the shared frame (widgets blueprint 1.0.0): logo tile and name, people waiting for kudos as the big number, who is waiting with their sport, early-riser badge and ×n, and "of 15 today, 10:22" at the bottom

The widget reads a summary saved on this iPhone, so it works offline; after the time set in Settings › Widget › "Mark the widget as out of date after" (12 h by default) its bottom line turns amber

releases.title: Catch up. Cheer. Move on.

highlights.title: A logo of its own
highlights.text: The route digest: a route from a teal start to a rose finish, with two digest lines.

highlights.title: Launch screen

highlights.title: Branded everywhere

Logo mark in the sticky header with "Digest" in the brand rose, the logo on an empty day, and at the top of the README

changes: Pace indicator after distance in the Compact and Tiny layouts

highlights.title: Tap to expand

highlights.title: See what's inside
highlights.text: Distance, trophies and photo counts on every line, so you know what's worth opening.

highlights.title: Tiny opens in place

changes: Compact layout folds each activity to its title, time and indicators; tap to expand or collapse
Indicators for distance (or time), achievements and photos, with PRs highlighted in gold
Tiny layout shows the same indicators and expands an athlete's activities in place
Expanded cards stay open while details load in the background
The details sheet always shows the full card

releases.title: Make it yours

highlights.title: Colours and layout
highlights.text: Six colour palettes or Auto, plus Comfortable, Compact or a one-line Tiny layout.

highlights.title: Text size and font
highlights.text: Pick Small to Larger text and a sans or serif font for names and titles.

highlights.title: Tune everything

fixes: Settings icon looked smaller than the refresh icon

highlights.title: Settings screen
